analysis.title: SharkNinja, Inc. (SN) 3Q26 Earnings Review: Broad-based momentum continues
key_insights: GS reiterates Buy on SN after a 3Q26 beat and a raised FY26 guide. Adjusted EPS of $2.34 compares with GS/FactSet consensus of $1.87/$1.89.
Net revenue grew 21.2% Y/Y (21.2% ex-FX) versus GS/consensus of +13.9%/+14.8%. Domestic sales rose 19.4% and International rose 25.2%.

Adjusted gross margin expanded about 560bps Y/Y to 55.9% versus GS/consensus of 54.3%, helped by tariff refunds. Adjusted opex was 34.4% of sales versus 35.0%/35.7% expected. Adjusted EBITDA margin was 23.3% versus 21.2%/21.1%.

FY26 adjusted EPS guidance was raised to $6.65-$6.75 from $6.45-$6.55, above GS/FactSet consensus of $6.53/$6.57. Sales growth guidance moved to 18.0%-19.0% from 16.0%-17.0%. Adjusted EBITDA guidance moved to $1.380bn-$1.391bn from $1.357bn-$1.369bn.

The high end of the guide implies about 17% 4Q revenue growth and 9% adjusted EBITDA growth. Adjusted gross margin is expected to fall about 100bps Y/Y in 4Q as tariff-refund reinvestments shift from 3Q into 4Q. Management says these investments are contained to 4Q.

GS lists four proof points. The base business is the largest contributor to 3Q growth, with US sales accelerating to +20.8%. International sales grew 25.2% and management expects growth to reaccelerate in 4Q. DTC is expected to grow faster than the overall business in 2027, with social commerce broadening reach. Management reiterated that adjusted EBITDA growth should outpace sales in 2027.

Margins are expected to be noisy because of commodity, fuel and FX headwinds and FY26 growth investments funded by a $134mn tariff refund benefit. The FY26 flow-through to EBITDA is $30mn. In 2027 management expects operating leverage to drive margin expansion, with AI investments in media and promotional spending as an additional lever.

Management frames SN as a consumer technology company with a TAM expanded to about $130bn and says double-digit growth is durable. GS expects future products to skew toward wellness and more technology-enhanced interfaces.

GS raises FY26/FY27/FY28 adjusted EPS to $6.78/$7.75/$8.71 from $6.53/$7.46/$8.39. The 12-month price target rises to $234 from $204 on a rolled-forward Q5-Q8 EV/EBITDA method and a higher target multiple of 18.85x versus 17.5x.

GS acknowledges that valuation will increasingly be debated after the stock's recent run. SN is up 91.0% over 6 months and 158.9% over 12 months. Price is $219.25 versus the $234 target, implying 6.7% upside.
Key downside risks named: wholesale and social-channel partner concentration, slowing innovation, corporate structure, and input costs, commodities and tariffs.

market_movers.rationale: Target raised from $204 on the 3Q beat, higher estimates and a higher target multiple of 18.85x EV/EBITDA. GS cites increased conviction in broad-based innovation-led growth.

earnings_insights: SN 3Q26 reported adjusted EPS $2.34 (printed 11/4 per the report's 4 November date) versus GS consensus est $1.87 and FactSet consensus est $1.89. The beat included a tariff refund benefit in gross margin.
3Q26 net revenue +21.2% Y/Y reported (21.2% ex-FX) versus GS est +13.9% and consensus est +14.8%. Domestic +19.4%, International +25.2%.
3Q26 adjusted gross margin 55.9% reported (+~560bps Y/Y) versus GS/consensus est 54.3%. Adjusted EBITDA margin 23.3% reported versus GS est 21.2% and consensus est 21.1%.

FY26 company guidance (new): adjusted EPS $6.65-$6.75 (prior $6.45-$6.55) versus GS est $6.53 and FactSet consensus est $6.57. Sales growth 18.0%-19.0% versus consensus est +17.0%/+17.4%. Adjusted EBITDA $1.380bn-$1.391bn versus consensus est $1.369bn/$1.367bn.
4Q26 implied by the high end of guidance: about 17% revenue growth and 9% adjusted EBITDA growth, with adjusted gross margin down about 100bps Y/Y.
GS estimates (adjusted diluted EPS): FY26E $6.78, FY27E $7.75, FY28E $8.71. Revenue estimates: FY26E $7,638.7mn, FY27E $8,674.2mn, FY28E $9,542.1mn. Prior GS EPS estimates were $6.53/$7.46/$8.39.
risk_factors: Valuation debate after the recent share price rise.
Noisy margins from commodity, fuel and FX headwinds and from 4Q tariff-refund reinvestments.

tension_points.bull_case: GS sees multiple avenues to compound growth. These are core momentum, adjacent category expansion, scaling of International and a stronger omnichannel model. Management says double-digit growth is durable and EBITDA growth should outpace sales in 2027.
tension_points.bear_case: GS acknowledges valuation will increasingly be debated after the recent appreciation. The shares trade at 32.4x FY26E P/E versus 19.0x for FY25. 2027 margins also face noisy commodity, fuel and FX headwinds and a tariff refund comparison.
tension_points.what_invalidates: The report names no level. It says the valuation debate raises the importance of continued execution.

theme_stances.key_argument: Core, International and omnichannel growth plus social commerce support continued compounding.
